date_note: Nextgov says the notice was published Monday (23 November) in the Federal Register; the proposals were first released 27 October.
exec: Makers of US Cyber Trust Mark smart devices may have to renew security certifications every three years; comments are due 23 December.
plain: The US FCC proposes that makers of smart devices carrying its Cyber Trust Mark security label renew their certification every three years, Nextgov reports.
summary: Nextgov reports that manufacturers would need to renew their products' Cyber Trust Mark security certifications every three years under an FCC proposal; a stakeholder committee had recommended five years. A notice published Monday in the Federal Register sets a 23 December deadline for public comments. The FCC is also considering more frequent checks after sale for baby monitors, home security cameras and products marketed to children.
title: FCC proposes three-year security renewals for Cyber Trust Mark products, Nextgov reports
